newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico approves Bell Atlantic control of Iusacell.
newsitem.headline: Mexico approves Bell Atlantic control of Iusacell.

text.p: The Mexican government has given the go-ahead for U.S.-based Bell Atlantic Corp to assume management control of Mexico's Grupo Iusacell SA de CV, Iusacell said on Thursday.
Iusacell said in a statement that it and Bell Atlantic, which reached agreement in principle regarding the change of control late last year, would close the transaction within the next week.

The deal will not change the economic ownership structure of the cellular telephone company, the statement said. Grupo Iusa, through the Peralta family, will continue to own 48 percent. Bell Atlantic will continue to own about 42 percent, with 10 percent remaining in the public's hands.

"This new structure, once it is finalized, will further position Grupo Iusacell as a formidable competitor in the new Mexican telecommunications marketplace," said Bell Atlantic Vice Chairman Lawrence Babbio.

When the deal was announced last November, Bell Atlantic agreed to pay a $50 million premium on voting A shares to Grupo Iusa in exchange for non-voting B and D shares. Bell Atlantic will also issue Iusacell $150 million in subordinated debentures, convertible to series A shares at $7 per ADS.

Bell Atlantic pushed to gain management control of the Mexican company after one of its owners, industrialist Carlos Peralta, was dogged by scandal last year involving a controversial payment of $50 million he admits he made to the jailed brother of ex-President Carlos Salinas, Raul. Peralta's tax returns have also been audited by the Finance Ministry.
The Peralta scandal set back Iusacell's timetable for obtaining a fixed wireless license from the Mexican government, analysts have said.
